messages.subject: Re: setDummyRef possible fix
messages.body_plain:
Sorry, scratch that, we now think we have identified the root cause. The Windows binary of httpuv that's on http://rstudio.org/_packages was built under R 3.0.1, and we're guessing everyone who has seen this problem is on R 3.0.0. I've rebuilt the httpuv binary on R 3.0.0, which should work with either R 3.0.0 or R 3.0.1.

So you should be able to fix this just by re-installing httpuv:

install.packages('httpuv', repos=c(RStudio='http://rstudio.org/_packages', CRAN='http://cran.rstudio.com'))

Please let us know if that does not fix it for you. Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
When you log into the AWS console and go to EC2 there should be a button on the left called Security Groups. Once you're there you can view all the Security Groups you've created (by default there's only one, called 'default'). Click on that, then go to Inbound on the window that appears, then add 3838 as the port range and click Add Rule, then Apply Rule Changes.

The page should look like this before you add it: http://imgur.com/zWSMQNl

Hope that works!

messages.subject_clean: problem: place an input$variable in SQL query
messages.body_plain:
Because of the problem with parameterized queries, I have switched to JDBC for shiny and other web-based applications. It's easy and amazingly fast. You must put the driver "sqljdbc4.jar" into you directory. Note that the dbSendPreparedQuery works for whole dataframes, and it is very fast. It also handles AutoIncrement columns, which always drops me back to by-row-Inserts in RODBC

> > library(RJDBC)
> > drv = JDBC("com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver", "sqljdbc4.jar")
> > con =  dbConnect(drv,"jdbc:sqlserver://localhost:64833;databaseName=MyDB",
> >           user = "user",password="mypassword")
> > vals = dbGetPreparedQuery(con, .... See documentation
> >
> >

> As I said, I don't know if RODBC provides an escaping function, or a way to do parameterized queries.
>

messages.subject: Re: Conditional Panel Issue (Newbie)
messages.body_plain:
1) You can't read dsdData and nsdData as if they are data frames. The return value from renderTable isn't a data frame; it's a value that is only useful for assigning to output$whatever. So if you want to access the data and use it from two or more places, you want to extract that part of the code and put it in a reactive expression. (Similar to how, in non-reactive code, you'd assign a variable.) Then you can access the value of that reactive expression from any other render or reactive code, by calling it as if it's a function. Like so:

dsdData <- reactive({
  # blah blah
  read.csv(dsdFile$datapath)
})

output$dsdData <- renderTable({ dsdData() })

output$dsdCheckBoxes <- renderUI({
  data <- dsdData()
  if (is.null(data)) return(NULL)
  dsdCheckBoxes <- names(data)

  checkboxGroupInput("dsdCheckBoxes", "Choose Variables", dsdCheckBoxes)

})

ui

})

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Concurrent Access & Feature List
messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael, great questions.

On Fri, May 24, 2013 at 8:50 AM, Michael Sevast <michael...@gmail.com> wrote:

> 1) Is concurrency limitation an issue with the beta of Shiny, or is this a limitation with R in general?
>          If Shiny, will the upcoming commercial version address this?

The issue is that R does not support concurrent execution. We plan to address this in the commercial version of Shiny by launching multiple R processes, up to 1 per user.

> 2) What are the differences between the beta today and the upcoming commercial version?  is there a link to see the upcoming features and/or history of the releases?

There isn't a public feature list. We intend to release a very early version of the commercial server in late June with simple authentication features, multiple R processes per app, and removal of the requirement to run the server as root. (That last feature will be upstreamed to the open source version as well.) Additional features will be in the final 1.0 release, mostly around security, monitoring, and scaling.

> 3) Once the commercial version is available, what will it cost and what will the support model look like?

We don't intend to charge for the preview version. Pricing for the final version and support are both TBD. If you want to contact me off-list I'd be very interested to hear what your needs and budget are.

You got it.

FYI, the session parameter is where we hang a bunch of (not yet documented?) information and functions that you might find useful; it is not for storing your own data. session$clientData contains metadata from the browser, session$sendCustomMessage/sendInputMessage/sendJavascript are used for sending various types of messages to the client, and session$onSessionEnded is used to register a callback for when the session is terminated (i.e. after the websocket closes).

messages.subject: Re: questions about a Shiny app using dynamic UI and reactiveValues
messages.subject_clean: questions about a Shiny app using dynamic UI and reactiveValues
messages.body_plain:
You actually don't need reactiveValues() at all if all you want is caching. Reactive expressions already have caching built-in. So in other words:

dataInput <- reactive({
  if (is.null(input$file))
    return(NULL)
  return(read.csv(input$file$datapath))
})

You can call dataInput() all over your code, and read.csv will only be executed a single time for each file that is uploaded.

To answer your original question anyway, reactive expressions (i.e. reactive({ ... }) ) should never be used to ASSIGN variables, whether reactive variables or non-reactive variables. You don't want them to have side effects because, as you've discovered, reactive expressions don't execute unless they are needed by an output or observer. The right way to assign variables in response to inputs/reactives changing, is to write an observer.

You can find out much more about observers and the rest in the Reactivity Overview <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview>.

messages.subject: Re: newbie questions
messages.body_plain:
First a general hint: If you are defining a reactive() inside of a renderXXX() or inside of another reactive(), you are probably making a mistake. Reactives and render functions should always be defined separately and refer to each other by name.

Here's a rewrite of your server.R:

library(shiny)
library(datasets)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  data_frame<-reactive({
    raw_data<-input$file1
    if(is.null(raw_data))
      return(NULL)

    read.csv(raw_data$datapath,header=input$header,sep=input$sep,quote=input$quote)
  })

  output$contents <- renderTable({

    if (is.null(data_frame()))
      return(NULL)

    read.csv(data_frame(), header=input$header, sep=input$sep, quote=input$quote)

  })

  output$boxplot<-renderPlot({
    data_Column<-input$data_column

    boxplot(data_frame()[,data_Column])
  })

  observe({
    if (is.null(data_frame()))
      return()
    updateCheckboxGroupInput(session, "variables", choices=names(data_frame()))
  })
})

Hi Andrew - if you're not using the latest development version, try updating to that. There have been some changes since dateInput was first implemented a few weeks back.

It now uses the current date on the client as the starting value, if 'value' is not specified. One drawback to using something like dateInput(..., value = Sys.date()) is that it will use the current date on the server, which may differ from the date on the client due to time zone differences. Also, I believe that ui.r will be run once and the output will be cached; that means that if you have an app that runs for more than a day, it will still keep printing out the start date even when new users connect. You could work around this by using updateDateInput() from server.R. But it's easier to just leave the date unspecified and let the client figure it out.

Another tool, let's call it X, which speaks to (an equivalent API to) the restful API can also download attachments, and downloads then to a well known location on the filesystem.

How do I use httr to download files and set their modification dates appropriately?  I'm sure Curl can do it, but I want to know how to do it cleanly using R apis.

Thanks,

-Alex

messages.body_plain:
I'm doing a Shiny application with some dynamic UI. In the first tab, the user uploads a file and choose the columns to be plotted.

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/stla/testDynamicUIdataplot/

An example csv data file is attached and is also available at https://www.dropbox.com/s/jkq147hqmrtrnq4/datGLIMMER2.csv

I encounter two problems:

- When uploading the file, a temporary error message appears, like :

Error in names(dat) <- ...
  'names' attribute [4] must be the same length as the vector [0]

  I'm under the impression this is a "synchronization" problem of the reactive process and the R code. Surely I could suppress this error message with the `try()` function, but is there a better way to solve this problem ?

- I misunderstand the practice of `reactiveValues()`. I'm trying to use `reactiveValues()` in order to store the loaded data in a R object, to avoid reading several times the csv file (for instance if I call the data with my `dataInput()` function the at each time it reads the csv file).
My `reactiveValues()` object is called `DATA`, it contains the two objects `dat0` and `dat`. I have noticed that I can directly call `DATA$dat0` but not `DATA$dat` (thus each time I want to get `DATA$dat` I call my function `wdatGet()`). Is it related to the fact that `dat0` appears in the output, but not `dat` ?
More importantly, could you please comment about the way to use `reactiveValues()` in order to store the loaded csv file ? Or maybe there's a more appropriaté way than using `reactiveValues` ?

```
## ui.R
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Control chart"),
#
  sidebarPanel(
    fileInput("file", "Data file (CSV)", multiple=FALSE),
    br(),
    uiOutput("select_date"),
    uiOutput("datelabel"),
    br(),
    uiOutput("select_LP"),
    uiOutput("LPlabel"),
    br(),
    uiOutput("select_HP"),
    uiOutput("HPlabel"),
    br(),
    uiOutput("select_group"),
    uiOutput("legend"),
    br(),
    radioButtons("transfo", "Transformation:",
                 list("Log" = "log",
                      "None" = "none")),
    br(),
    checkboxInput("calibration", "Calibration period"),
    helpText("this must be a 0/1 column"),
    conditionalPanel(
      condition = "input.calibration == true",
      uiOutput("select_calibration"))
  ),
  mainPanel(
    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Data",
               h3("Data file:"),
               textOutput("loaded"),
               tableOutput("filetable"),
               div(class="container-fluid", style="overflow:auto;background-color:#FFD700;height:150px;",
                   div(class="row-fluid",
                       div(class="span12", tableOutput("dat"))
                   )
               ),
               #h3("Plot of data:"),
               div(class="container-fluid", style="overflow:auto;height:800px;",
                   plotOutput("plotdata")
               )
               ),
      tabPanel("Not implemented yet",
               h3("xxx")
      ),
      id="idtab"
    )
  )
))
```

```
# setwd("~/Work/RD/QC Charts")
## server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  ##
  ## load data file
  ##
  fileInput <- reactive( {
    if (is.null(input$file)) {
      # User has not uploaded a file yet
      return(NULL)
    }
    input$file
  })
  ##
  ## output message : file loaded
  ##
  output$loaded <- reactive({
    if (is.null(input$file)) {
      # User has not uploaded a file yet
      return("no file loaded yet")
    }
    ""
  })
  ##
  ## output : show loaded file
  ##
  output$filetable <- renderTable({
    fileInput()
  })
  ##
  ## read data file
  ##
  DATA <- reactiveValues()
  dataInput <- reactive({
    if (is.null(input$file)) {
      # User has not uploaded a file yet
      return(NULL)
    }
    inFile <- input$file
    dat0 <- read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=T)
    DATA$dat0 <- dat0
    dat0
  })
  ##
  ## output: print contents of loaded file
  ##
  output$dat <- renderTable({
    dataInput()
  })
  ##
  ## Variables selection
  ##
  output$select_date <- renderUI({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)) return(NULL)
    factors <- names(dat)[sapply(dat, class) == "factor"]
    ok <- tolower(factors) %in% c("date", "time")
    selected <- ifelse(any(ok), factors[which(ok)[1]], factors[1])
    selectInput(inputId = 'col.date',
                label = "Select date:",
                choices = factors,
                selected = selected
    )
  })
  output$datelabel <- renderUI({
    if(is.null(DATA$dat0)) return(NULL)
    textInput("datelabel", "x-axis label:", value=input$col.date)
  })
  output$select_group <- renderUI({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)) return(NULL)
    factors <- names(dat)[sapply(dat, class) == "factor"]
    ok <- tolower(factors) %in% c("tech")
    selected <- ifelse(any(ok), factors[which(ok)[1]], factors[1])
    selectInput(inputId = 'col.group',
                label = "Select coloring group:",
                choices = factors,
                selected = selected
    )
  })
  output$legend <- renderUI({
    if(is.null(DATA$dat0)) return(NULL)
    textInput("legend", "Legend title:", value=input$col.group)
  })
  output$select_LP <- renderUI({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)) return(NULL)
    numerics <- names(dat)[sapply(dat, class) != "factor"]
    ok <- tolower(numerics) %in% c("lp", "cp1")
    selected <- ifelse(any(ok), numerics[which(ok)[1]], numerics[1])
    selectInput(inputId = 'col.LP',
                label = "Select low control:",
                choices = numerics,
                selected = selected
    )
  })
  output$LPlabel <- renderUI({
    if(is.null(DATA$dat0)) return(NULL)
    textInput("LPlabel", "y-axis label for low control:", value=input$col.LP)
  })
  output$select_HP <- renderUI({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)) return(NULL)
    numerics <- names(dat)[sapply(dat, class) != "factor"]
    ok <- tolower(numerics) %in% c("hp", "cp2")
    selected <- ifelse(any(ok), numerics[which(ok)[1]], numerics[2])
    selectInput(inputId = 'col.HP',
                label = "Select high control:",
                choices = numerics,
                selected = selected
    )
  })
  output$HPlabel <- renderUI({
    if(is.null(DATA$dat0)) return(NULL)
    textInput("HPlabel", "y-axis label for high control:", value=input$col.HP)
  })
  output$select_calibration <- renderUI({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)) return(NULL)
    numerics <- names(dat)[sapply(dat, class) != "factor"]
    ok <- tolower(numerics) %in% c("range", "reference", "calibration")
    selected <- ifelse(any(ok), numerics[which(ok)[1]], numerics[1])
    selectInput(inputId = 'col.calibration',
                label = "Calibration indicator:",
                choices = numerics,
                selected = selected
    )
  })
  ##
  ## create dataframe with generic variable names
  ##
  wdatGet <- reactive({
    dat <- DATA$dat0
    if(is.null(dat)){ return(NULL) }
    if(input$calibration){
        dat <- subset(dat, select=c(input$col.date,input$col.LP,input$col.HP,input$col.calibration,input$col.group))
        names(dat) <- c("Date", "LP", "HP", "calib", "group")
        dat$pch <- 19
        if(all(dat$calib) %in% c(0,1)){
          dat[which(dat$calib==1),"pch"] <- 23
        }
    }else{
        dat <- subset(dat, select=c(input$col.date,input$col.LP,input$col.HP,input$col.group))
        names(dat) <- c("Date", "LP", "HP", "group")
        dat$pch <- 19
    }
    dat$color <- as.numeric(dat$group)
    dat$mydate <- as.Date(dat[,"Date"], "%d/%m/%Y")
    dat$dateID <- as.numeric(dat$mydate)
    f <- switch(input$transfo, none=function(x) x, log=log)
    dat <- transform(dat, LP=f(LP), HP=f(HP))
    dat <- droplevels(subset(dat, subset= !is.na <http://is.na>(LP) & !is.na <http://is.na>(HP) & !is.na <http://is.na>(date)))
    DATA$wdat <- dat
  })
  ####
  #### PLOT DATA
  ####
  output$plotdata <- renderPlot({
    wdatGet()
    dat <- DATA$wdat
    if (is.null(input$file)) {
        # User has not uploaded a file yet
      return(NULL)
    }
    d <- dat$mydate
    x <- dat$LP
    y <- dat$HP
    k <- 1.08 # factor for ylim (default =1.08)
    par(mfrow=c(2,1),mar=c(6,3,3,3))
    r <- x
    ylims <- (max(r)-diff(range(r))/2) + c(-1,1) * diff(range(r)) * k/2
    plot(d,x,type="p",xaxt="n",
         xlab=NA, ylab="LP",
         col=dat$group,
         ylim=ylims,
         pch=dat$pch,bg="gold")
    at <- seq(d[1], d[length(d)], length.out=25)
    axis.Date(1, at = at,
              labels = at,
              format= "%d/%m/%Y", las = 2)
    r <- y
    ylims <- (max(r)-diff(range(r))/2) + c(-1,1) * diff(range(r)) * k/2
    plot(d,y,type="p",xaxt="n",
         xlab=NA, ylab="LP",
         col=dat$group,
         ylim=ylims,
         pch=dat$pch,bg="yellow2")
    axis.Date(1, at = at,
              labels = at,
              format= "%d/%m/%Y", las = 2)
  },  height=800)
})
```

messages.subject: Re: Role of invalidateLater
messages.body_plain:
Very cool.

Yes, you would use invalidateLater to automatically retrieve data periodically. If the data can be shared between all users, then you could do this outside of the server function.

sharedValues <- reactiveValues()
observe({
  invalidateLater(600000)  # ten minutes
  sharedValues$data <- retrieveData()  # or whatever you do to get the data
})

Elsewhere in your app, just refer to sharedValues$data. (Be sure to check for NULL for the startup case)

This is a less obvious approach than simply doing this:

sharedData <- reactive({
  invalidateLater(60000)
  retrieveData()
})

and referring to sharedData() elsewhere; but the observer/reactiveValues approach is superior because if the value doesn't change from the previous value, then sharedValues$data does not invalidate its dependencies.

messages.body_plain:
John, grey-outs from long server processing is a feature, not a bug--it shows the user what output(s) are being recalculated. If you don't like it you can override the CSS to have a different, or no, effect. This is what the original CSS rule looks like:
.recalculating {
  opacity: 0.3;
  transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
  -moz-transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
  -webkit-transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
  -o-transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
}
You can apply your own styles for .recalculating to change the opacity to 1 and then do other stuff instead.

messages.subject: problem with R package 'gbm' in Shiny app
messages.subject_clean: problem with R package 'gbm' in Shiny app
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am working on a Shiny app using gradient boosting, via the gbm package and am encounter a problem. I am simply trying to use the example code visible by looking up the gbm function, ?gbm. Specifically, running the example code to simulate the data and then create the object 'gbm1'. There is a discrepancy between running the example in an ordinary R session on my desktop vs. creating the same gbm object within a Shiny app.

It turns out, as long as the argument to gbm, 'cv.folds',  is set as cv.folds=1 (no cross-validation), it will work in Shiny. But if I set it to two or higher, the example still works fine in an ordinary R session but not within a Shiny app. I believe this is because the use of cross validation invokes some otherwise ignored nested functions within the gbm call which eventually invoke the base R 'parallel' package, in an attempt to detect multiple cores for sending different cross-validation folds to. This is visible by following the breadcrumb trail of the n.cores argument in the gbm function. It gets passed down through gbmCrossVal to gbmCrossValModelBuild to gbmCluster, where n.cores is finally used. However, I set n.cores=1 in the main gbm call to avoid any parallelization. But in any case, I get an error anytime cv.folds is greater than one., e.g. "2 nodes produced errors; first error: incorrect number of dimensions" where "2" is because I used cv.folds=2 this time.

I don't know if this is a Shiny problem, a gbm problem (in the sense that it works fine apart from Shiny but perhaps was not coded up in a way that will play nice with Shiny). Invariably when I see something like "incorrect number of dimensions" that is a clear indication it's probably user error and I have a typo somewhere. But in this case, it's the gbm package example code, and it runs fine when not built into a Shiny app. I apologize if this questions is a bit too esoteric for this venue. But hopefully whatever the problem is, it turns out to be a more general issue and doesn't have to do with gbm specifically, perhaps something with its attempted use of the parallel package, i.e. makeCluster and parLapply.

Thanks,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: Installing ImageMagick tools on glimmer
messages.body_plain:
I think you want to write the video file into a subdirectory of your app called "www" (if it doesn't have one, create one). The name of the subdirectory MUST be "www".

Then use renderUI instead of renderImage. Your renderUI block should return a video tag like so:

tags$video(src=filename, width="640", height="480")

The filename is the bare filename of the video file, i.e. do NOT include "www".

Then in ui.R use uiOutput or htmlOutput instead of imageOutput.

I have tried working with this in the past. The main issue is that DataTables expects tables to contain thead and tbody tags clearly outlining the column headers from the body.

Unfortunately, none of the R packages (xtable, hwriter, R2HTML) use this markup, as a result of which the DataTables plugin is unable to style these tables.

It should be fairly straightforward patching the code in any of these packages, however I am not sure if any of them are under active development.

Best,
Ramnath

Today, you would have to handle the click on a table cell manually using jQuery. $(document).on('click', 'table#foo td', function(e) { ... }) or whatever.

To route the value to the server, yes, send it using JavaScript (the quick and dirty way being Shiny.shinyapp.sendInput({name: value}), but we should have better ways to do this soon). I recommend having your value be an object that includes a nonce (could just be monotonically increasing number) and the data i.e. table cell that was clicked, if you care about responding to multiple clicks on the same cell. (If this is just driving selection then no need for the nonce)

As for adding a tab to the tabset, I'm not sure how this works in Bootstrap. If it's possible in JS then you can use session$sendInputMessage.

Here is the version with avconv :  http://glimmer.rstudio.com/stla/testVideoavconv/ (with the webm format => Chrome only)

# server R
library(animation)
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$video <- renderUI({
    n <- input$n
    videoname <- "gaussian.webm"

    outdir <- "~/ShinyApps/testVideoavconv/www"

    saveVideo({
      for (i in 1:n) {
        curve(dnorm(x), from = -4, to = 4)
        set.seed(666)
        simulation <- rnorm(i)
        points(x = simulation, y = rep(0, i), col = "red", pch = 19)
      }

    }, video.name <http://video.name> = videoname, outdir = outdir, ffmpeg="avconv")

    tags$video(src=videoname, width="640", height="480", type='video/webm; codecs="vp8.0, vorbis"', controls="controls")
  })
})

On Wednesday, May 29, 2013 4:57:14 PM UTC-8, Matthew Leonawicz wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I am working on a Shiny app using gradient boosting, via the gbm package and am encounter a problem. I am simply trying to use the example code visible by looking up the gbm function, ?gbm. Specifically, running the example code to simulate the data and then create the object 'gbm1'. There is a discrepancy between running the example in an ordinary R session on my desktop vs. creating the same gbm object within a Shiny app.
>
> It turns out, as long as the argument to gbm, 'cv.folds',  is set as cv.folds=1 (no cross-validation), it will work in Shiny. But if I set it to two or higher, the example still works fine in an ordinary R session but not within a Shiny app. I believe this is because the use of cross validation invokes some otherwise ignored nested functions within the gbm call which eventually invoke the base R 'parallel' package, in an attempt to detect multiple cores for sending different cross-validation folds to. This is visible by following the breadcrumb trail of the n.cores argument in the gbm function. It gets passed down through gbmCrossVal to gbmCrossValModelBuild to gbmCluster, where n.cores is finally used. However, I set n.cores=1 in the main gbm call to avoid any parallelization. But in any case, I get an error anytime cv.folds is greater than one., e.g. "2 nodes produced errors; first error: incorrect number of dimensions" where "2" is because I used cv.folds=2 this time.
>
> I don't know if this is a Shiny problem, a gbm problem (in the sense that it works fine apart from Shiny but perhaps was not coded up in a way that will play nice with Shiny). Invariably when I see something like "incorrect number of dimensions" that is a clear indication it's probably user error and I have a typo somewhere. But in this case, it's the gbm package example code, and it runs fine when not built into a Shiny app. I apologize if this questions is a bit too esoteric for this venue. But hopefully whatever the problem is, it turns out to be a more general issue and doesn't have to do with gbm specifically, perhaps something with its attempted use of the parallel package, i.e. makeCluster and parLapply.
>
> Thanks,
> Matt

messages.subject: Re: Default library in linux server
messages.body_plain:
You either need to "sudo su --login" (to install as root, into /usr/local/lib/R/site-library) or "sudo su --login shiny" (to install into the "shiny" user's personal library, assuming you even gave the shiny user a home directory).

Here's the one-liner to install forecast as root into the site-library:

sudo su --login -c "R -e \"install.packages('forecast', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""

messages.subject: Re: storing a dataframe
messages.body_plain:
I sort-of understand what you are doing now. A couple of pointers:
If no file is selected, make.eval.table() raises an error, and thus an error occurs in observe({}). Apparently, in Shiny, if an error happens in an unprotected observer, the session ends. I'm not currently sure whether to categorize this as a feature or bug, but I'm leaning toward feature, as we have no idea what you intended in the observer and whether it is critical to the app.

You have a couple of approaches you can use to deal with this. The one more commonly espoused on this list is to detect the conditions where an error might occur, and have your reactive expressions return NULL. For example, you read input$file$datafile in a bunch of reactive expressions, without checking if a file is even selected. If you change these all to check for NULL first, and return NULL immediately, the app no longer errors. I made these changes and the app seems to stop crashing; if you can't figure out the changes for yourself let me know and I'll try to send you a patch file.

In your case, you have a LOT of reactive expressions, and many outputs as well; you may want to consider the second approach which is to catch the error at the observer/render methods (i.e. try() or tryCatch()). It depends on how you want to approach the problem I guess.

Avoid the use of periods in input/output IDs. This may cause problems on the JavaScript side, since periods are not allowed in JavaScript identifiers.

messages.subject: Scoping of reactive dependencies, reactive rain checks
messages.subject_clean: Scoping of reactive dependencies, reactive rain checks
messages.body_plain:
Hi

  I'm daresay that reactive depdendency tracking is done using dynamic scoping - that is to say if a reactive value (input) is consumed then the nearest reactive on the (parent frame) stack is assumed to have caused it.

  In R, I can evaluate functions in the scope of the caller.  For instance, to allow me to specify which specific columns in xtable are 'sanitized', I create a magic function which can see the internals of xtable:

noSanitize<-function(exclude)function(col){
 xtableLogic <- substitute(
  {if (names(x)[i] %in% exclude) col else sanitize(col)},
  list(exclude=exclude,col=col))
 eval(envir=parent.frame(),xtableLogic)
}

  I'm considering building an R asynchronous GET to streamline parallel fetches from shiny server to restful apis (and other ajax).

  For this I may require telling the caller of the asynchronous get that it should be re-evaluated, using the invalidatelater reactive.

  This is probably the wrong way to do it, but I want the user interface to be pretty (if not clean :) and want to explore some ideas.

 output$foo <- reactivePlot({ plot(parallelGet(input$url)) })

  How does the shiny reactive dependency tracker understand this?

  Would exceptions be a better way?

  stop(setClass(list(state="not ready",delay=ms(1)),"reactiveRainCheck"))

  (having shiny core understand this message to mean it should try the reactive again soon)

  Perhaps monads and infinite lists are a better idea, but I don't know where those are up to (if anywhere)

-Alex

Am Freitag, 31. Mai 2013 08:17:31 UTC+2 schrieb Joe Cheng [RStudio]:
> I sort-of understand what you are doing now. A couple of pointers:
> If no file is selected, make.eval.table() raises an error, and thus an error occurs in observe({}). Apparently, in Shiny, if an error happens in an unprotected observer, the session ends. I'm not currently sure whether to categorize this as a feature or bug, but I'm leaning toward feature, as we have no idea what you intended in the observer and whether it is critical to the app.
>
> You have a couple of approaches you can use to deal with this. The one more commonly espoused on this list is to detect the conditions where an error might occur, and have your reactive expressions return NULL. For example, you read input$file$datafile in a bunch of reactive expressions, without checking if a file is even selected. If you change these all to check for NULL first, and return NULL immediately, the app no longer errors. I made these changes and the app seems to stop crashing; if you can't figure out the changes for yourself let me know and I'll try to send you a patch file.
>
> In your case, you have a LOT of reactive expressions, and many outputs as well; you may want to consider the second approach which is to catch the error at the observer/render methods (i.e. try() or tryCatch()). It depends on how you want to approach the problem I guess.
>
> Avoid the use of periods in input/output IDs. This may cause problems on the JavaScript side, since periods are not allowed in JavaScript identifiers.

messages.subject: (devel version of shiny) removal of sendJavascript
messages.subject_clean: (devel version of shiny) removal of sendJavascript
messages.body_plain:
This is only relevant for people who are using the development version of Shiny, and are using the sendJavascript function from it.

I don't know if anyone has actually made use of the sendJavascript function, but if you are using it, you should know that it's been removed, because it does something that's hacky: it allows you to send Javascript code from the server, to be evaluated on the client.

If you need this functionality, you can easily add a custom message handler which has the same effect, using only a few lines of code. There's a minimal example app at:
https://github.com/wch/testapp/tree/master/sendjs

-Winston
